parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes universal-exposure measures at entry: passport/visa sex scrutiny with refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for document discrepancies, plus state-level facility exclusion across ~21 jurisdictions with criminal triggers in 4 and a documented arrest (24h in men's ward, 60-day misdemeanour). Documented custody abuse — forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse in immigration detention, conversion-model corrections policies — is a severe tier-1/tier-2 feature, and state threat-framing ('radical gender ideology' in counterterrorism guidance) raises outing stakes. Mitigations are real but partial: national employment ruling and hate-crime statute, ~30 states without facility bans, courts enjoining several orders, active litigation. No execution pathway; imprisonment possible but not near-certain. Sits between the 0.35 exclusion-regime anchors and the 0.55 administrative-friction anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal: passport marker rules force sex-at-birth disclosure; visa cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and considers lifetime fraud ineligibility; reports of confiscated passports and stranded travellers; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waivers, never automatic; policy under active court challenge.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry discrepancy can escalate from refusal to fraud investigation and immigration custody, feeding the documented abusive detention regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections adopting hair-cutting/hormone-withdrawal policies; transgender prisoner counts suppressed.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Habeas/consular access not documented for visitors; some orders enjoined in court; none shown remedying custody conditions.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry screening or visa fraud allegations channel travellers into this custody system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Universal-exposure: state facility bans in ~21 jurisdictions (government buildings/schools), 4 states criminalising; documented arrest of trans woman in women's restroom, 24h men's-ward hold; this state bans facility use in schools and state buildings effective July 2025.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart; ~29 states and capital district have no mapped ban; national law a backstop for employment only.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor outed at entry or check-in faces facility restriction throughout the stay in this state.

care_services.exposure: This state bans gender-affirming care for under-18s with forced tapering and civil liability to age 25; national proposed rules bar public insurance reimbursement; hospital-record subpoenas for patients under 19 chill care-seeking.
care_services.protection: Litigation ongoing against national health rules; state contract termination remedied by settlement after lawsuit.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and possible investigation exposure; adult emergency care exposure not documented but subpoenas raise doubt.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing: 'gender ideology' removals, DOJ cash-reward memorandum naming 'radical gender ideology', counterterrorism strategy prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 2023 wave of 190+ anti-trans bills; state among worst-ranked for adult-targeting legislation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; counterterrorism guidance disclaims targeting mere disagreement; advocates litigating.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing licenses street-level and bureaucratic hostility toward outed visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: National order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a minor's social transition (names/pronouns); state care ban for under-18s; 27 states ban minor care; school-facility exclusion applies to travelling minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Some orders enjoined; marriage and employment recognition untouched; litigation pending.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor risks the minor's care denial and third-party investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One documented arrest under a bathroom law with men's-ward hold; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity; business-service denial statute permits refusal to LGBTQ people.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute (2009) and 2020 employment ruling backstop; scattered municipal protections; tribal hate-crime law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are plausible outers via documents; national backstop exists but enforcement for visitors not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement of the state facilities law in custody unresolved; whether licence marker changes remain operative after the March 2026 ruling unsourced; risk map flags 4 'Do Not Travel' states for trans people.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ guides documentation; courts have overturned or enjoined multiple measures; settlement obtained against the state for discriminatory contract termination.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are litigation-dependent, slow, and mostly not demonstrated to resolve a visitor's live crisis.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra excludes and humiliates without custody; here exposure includes documented custodial abuse (immigration detention sexual violence, corrections conversion model), criminal bathroom triggers with a real arrest, and lifetime fraud bars — materially worse operative severity than 0.35-A, though both share universal, remedy-light document/facility regimes.

Tarnov's private-gatekeeper verification and occasional administrative holds match the document-mismatch and facility-scrutiny exposure here, with custodial prosecution rare in both. This dossier adds documented detention abuse and state threat-framing, but also broader court injunctions and national anti-discrimination backstops; roughly comparable, marginally harsher on the custody axis.

Kestrel Isles' secondary screening, discretionary refusal of entry and weak real-time remedies mirror the border regime here, but Kestrel Isles lacks criminal facility triggers, documented trans-specific custody abuse and hostile counterterrorism framing; those tier-1/tier-2 features hold this jurisdiction below 0.55 despite comparable partial protections.

Ostravia's birth-sex custody placement and cross-dressing arrest statute parallel this jurisdiction's facility arrests and prison risks, but Ostravia's exposure is near-universal with weak courts; here ~30 states impose no facility ban, courts actively enjoin orders, and national hate-crime/employment protections operate, placing this clearly above 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime chains together: entry documents force sex-at-birth disclosure and permit refusal or fraud findings; a discrepancy can route a traveller into immigration custody with documented forced labour, sexual abuse and hormone withdrawal; and within the state, 2025 facility law excludes trans visitors from school and state-building facilities, with a criminal trespass trigger elsewhere and a documented handcuffed arrest and men's-ward hold. A travelling minor faces care bans and prosecution threats to facilitators. These are universal-exposure and tier-1/tier-2 features. Countervailing protections — national employment and hate-crime backstops, ~30 ban-free states, enjoined orders, active litigation — are genuine but largely do not resolve a visitor's live crisis. Net: elevated-to-high risk, ~0.44.
